title: 4a. 50M edges: the cost model takes over
subtitle: The planner asked for 500 betweenness pivots; the cost model cut it to 125 to fit the budget; the run finished in 20 minutes.
note: Scene 4 of 4: recorded on a 10M-node, 50M-edge graph. See the cost model decision under Cost.

tier_notes: s1: betweenness pivots reduced to 125 to stay within budget

plan.rationale: The user named betweenness and accepted an approximation, so no alternative measure is needed. Pivot-sampled betweenness on this very large, connected, undirected, unweighted graph is used, and the top 10 nodes are ranked.

findings.detail: relative error on top ranks typically < 10% with 125 pivots on graphs of this size; exact values would need O(nm)=5.0e+14 operations

result.explanation: The 10 nodes with the highest approximate betweenness centrality are, in descending order: 6 (≈2079528851414.5), 9 (≈1565041241613.3), 3 (≈1255177565069.7), 2 (≈1122391405127.5), 1 (≈944084575713.6), 42 (≈932450991620.0), 4 (≈909438597469.7), 15 (≈842947370356.7), 11 (≈637775809197.7) and 23 (≈584751885549.7). These come from pivot-sampled betweenness on the full graph (10,000,000 nodes), treated as undirected and unweighted, with no largest-component filtering. To stay within the compute budget, the sample was reduced to 125 pivots; exact betweenness would need about 5.0e+14 operations. At this sample size, relative error on the top ranks is typically under 10%, so close pairs such as nodes 1, 42 and 4 could swap places. Verification found no problems: all values are within the theoretical bound of 49999985000001.0.
